title: One customer config, 85% of a network
oneLine: A valid customer configuration change set off a bug shipped weeks earlier, and 85% of Fastly's network started returning errors.

facts.label: Network returning errors
facts.quote: which caused 85% of our network to return errors

facts.label: Time to detect
facts.quote: We detected the disruption within one minute

facts.label: Back to 95% normal
facts.quote: Within 49 minutes, 95% of our network was operating as normal.

facts.label: Bug shipped
facts.quote: On May 12, we began a software deployment that introduced a bug

events.label: Monitoring catches it
events.quote: Global disruption identified by Fastly monitoring

events.label: Customer config identified
events.quote: Fastly Engineering identified the customer configuration

levers.label: Rollout
levers.why: One customer's valid config reached the whole network
levers.quote: a customer pushed a valid configuration change that included the specific circumstances that triggered the bug

levers.label: Bug caught in testing
levers.why: The bug shipped on May 12 and waited for the right config
levers.quote: We'll figure out why we didn't detect the bug during our software quality assurance and testing processes.

levers.label: Alert to recovery
levers.why: Finding which customer configuration set it off took most of the time
levers.quote: We'll evaluate ways to improve our remediation time.

afterwards.quote: We're deploying the bug fix across our network as quickly and safely as possible.
We'll figure out why we didn't detect the bug during our software quality assurance and testing processes.
We'll evaluate ways to improve our remediation time.
fully leveraging the isolation capabilities of WebAssembly and Compute@Edge to build greater resiliency from the ground up

assumptions.what: Service comes back with a 490 second time constant once the change is pulled
assumptions.why: Fitted so the replay is back by 11:00, as the postmortem reports.

assumptions.what: The change reaches every server within a few seconds
assumptions.why: The postmortem does not say how fast it spread.

assumptions.what: Each staged rollout step waits 10 minutes, and early stages carry 1 to 2% of traffic each
assumptions.why: Used only when you switch the rollout to staged. The postmortem does not describe a staged path.
